title: How to Bleed a Radiator

seo.title: How to Bleed a Radiator
seo.meta_description: Bleed a radiator only when the hydronic system is designed for it: stop the heat, open the bleed valve carefully until water runs steadily, then check system pressure.
seo.search_intent: Release trapped air from a hot-water radiator in a controlled way and recognize when pressure, valve, circulation, or leakage is the real problem.

excerpt: A radiator that is warm at the bottom and cool at the top can contain air, but not every cold radiator needs bleeding. Confirm that it is a hot-water radiator with an accessible bleed valve.
content_html:
This procedure is for hot-water radiators with a designed bleed valve. It does not apply to electric radiators or steam systems without following their specific instructions.

Turn the heating off and let it settle

Avoid opening a bleed point while a pump is moving very hot water. Wait until the radiator is safe to handle and place a cloth or cup beneath the valve.

Open the valve only slightly

Use the correct key and turn slowly. Trapped air usually produces a hiss. Do not remove the bleed screw completely.

Close when water runs steadily

Once the air stops and a stable small flow appears, close the valve without overtightening. Dry the area and verify that it does not drip.

Check system pressure when applicable

Bleeding can lower pressure. Use the boiler/system manual for the correct range; do not refill blindly or operate valves you cannot identify.

Repeated air is a diagnostic clue

Frequent bleeding can point to incorrect pressure, leakage, expansion-vessel problems, or air entering the system. A completely cold radiator can also have a closed valve or circulation issue.

Bleeding is a specific fix for trapped air, not a task to repeat on a schedule without symptoms.

faq.question: How can I tell if there is air in the radiator?
faq.answer: A common pattern is cooler at the top and warmer at the bottom, sometimes with gurgling.

faq.question: Should I bleed it while the heating is running?
faq.answer: Follow the system manual; generally stop circulation and let the radiator reach a safe temperature first.

faq.question: Why did system pressure drop afterward?
faq.answer: Releasing air and a little water can change pressure; check the manufacturer’s specified range before adding water.
